studio.lead: A small studio in Tenerife. Here I paint watercolours on paper and ceramics on tableware — one pair of hands, one piece at a time, never mass-produced.
studio.workspaceImageAlt: Anna Ciok's ceramics studio in Tenerife
studio.storyH: I paint. On paper, and on ceramics.
studio.storyP1: I’m Anna. I am a painter and a ceramicist — to me it is one practice, not two separate ones. I paint in ink and watercolour on paper, then carry the same gestures and motifs onto tableware, which I glaze and fire.
studio.storyP2: I came to ceramics slowly: first a course, then a shelf in someone else’s studio, and finally my own small place — a glazing table and a painting corner side by side, plus a kiln. It is calm, physical work, and it refuses to be rushed.
studio.storyP3: I paint by hand, without transfers or stencils — on paper or on a piece alike. That is why a line sometimes wanders, a palm leans a little, and two similar motifs are never truly the same. The paper compositions enter a fine art edition as prints; the ceramics stays one of a kind — but in both, that is where the object starts to feel alive.
studio.fact1D: One room: paints and paper on one table, glaze and a kiln right next to it.
studio.fact2D: After painting and glazing, the ceramics goes into the kiln, where the firing sets the colour and turns the surface into a glassy, functional layer.
studio.fact3D: Some compositions stay on paper and enter a fine art edition. Others I glaze and fire as ceramics. The source is the same — one brush, one studio.
studio.fact4D: I pack and ship ceramics myself within 1–3 business days across Poland. Fine art prints are made and shipped by our partner Prodigi, usually within 5–10 days, anywhere in the EU or UK.
studio.procH: From the first line to a finished piece.
studio.p1P: Every piece starts as a drawing or a watercolour composition on paper — I plan the layout, choose the colours, and work without transfers, layer by layer.
studio.p2P: Some compositions stay on paper and enter a fine art edition as prints. The rest I carry onto tableware: I apply glaze and paint the motif by hand, straight onto the ceramic.
studio.p3P: Ceramics I fire in the kiln at 1040°C, look over carefully, and sign on the base. Fine art prints are printed on paper and shipped by our partner Prodigi.
studio.ctaH: One studio, two ways to live with art.
studio.ctaP: Ceramics exist only once — when a piece finds its home, it leaves the shop for good. Fine art prints are made to order, so the composition you love can always hang in yours.

shipping.lead: How I pack, how long the parcel takes, and what to do if a piece arrives damaged. Everything before you click “buy”.
shipping.s1P: I ship by InPost Parcel Locker (from 20 zł) or courier (30 zł) across all of Poland. Shipping costs the same regardless of how many pieces you order — if you buy several, they travel together in one parcel.
shipping.s1Li1: InPost Parcel Locker, all of Poland — from 20 zł
shipping.s1Li1b: InPost courier, all of Poland — 30 zł
shipping.s1Li3: International shipping — write to me and I’ll arrange it individually
shipping.s2P: The June-drop pieces are finished and already waiting in Poland, so there’s no production time. I send the parcel within 1–3 business days of the payment clearing, and the courier usually delivers the next day.
shipping.s2Note: I pack everything myself, between studio work and the next firings. If you need a specific date, write to me and I’ll check what is possible.
shipping.s3P: The ceramics travel wrapped by hand — film, cardboard and plenty of padding so nothing moves. I label the box as fragile. I try to limit plastic wherever I can, without risking the piece.
shipping.s4P: Live in Warsaw or passing through? You can collect your order in person — then shipping is free. We arrange the pickup by email for a specific day and time; this is not a fixed-hours pickup point.
shipping.s5P: As a consumer you have the right to withdraw from the purchase within 14 days of receiving the parcel, with no reason needed. You can start your return on the returns page — just your order number. You can also write to hej@ciok.art.
shipping.s5Li1: The piece should come back undamaged, ideally in its original packaging
shipping.s5Li2: The cost of return shipping is on the buyer
shipping.s5Li3: I refund within 14 days of receiving the piece back
shipping.s6P: Ceramics can be fragile, and couriers vary. If a parcel arrives broken, please photograph the contents and the packaging and send the photos to me the same day. I’ll replace the piece with another from the drop or refund the full amount including shipping — your choice.

terms.lead: The rules for buying at Anna Ciok Ceramics. Written plainly, without the legal fog — so you can actually read them.
terms.s1P1: The Anna Ciok Ceramics online shop is run by the ceramics studio of Anna Ciok, based in Warsaw. You can contact the seller at <link>hej@ciok.art</link>.
terms.s1P2: The items for sale are hand-painted ceramic pieces. Each piece is the only copy — once sold it disappears from the offer and is not remade.
terms.s2P: You place an order by adding selected pieces to the cart and confirming the purchase. The sale contract is concluded the moment the order is confirmed and the payment clears.
terms.s2Li1: Because each piece is unique, any given piece can be sold only once
terms.s2Li2: If for reasons beyond my control I cannot fulfil an order, I inform you immediately and refund the full amount
terms.s3P: All prices are given in Polish złoty (PLN) and are gross prices. The shipping cost shown in the cart before you confirm is added to the order total. Payment is handled by a secure external payment provider, Stripe.
terms.s4P: I send orders within 1–3 business days of the payment clearing. Details of costs, timing and pickup are described on the <link>Shipping & returns</link> page.
terms.s5P: A consumer has the right to withdraw from the purchase within 14 days of receiving the piece, without giving a reason. The statement can simply be sent by email. The returned piece should be undamaged; the buyer covers the return shipping, and the refund is made within 14 days.
terms.s6P: If a piece arrives damaged or not as described, you can file a complaint by email, attaching photos. I review it within 14 days and — depending on your choice — replace the piece or refund the full amount including shipping.
terms.s7P: Matters not covered by these terms are governed by Polish law, including the Consumer Rights Act and the Civil Code. Any changes to the terms do not affect orders placed before they take effect.

privacy.lead: What data I collect, what for, and for how long. Short, because there isn’t much data — this is a small studio, not a corporation.
privacy.s1P: The controller of your data is the ceramics studio of Anna Ciok, based in Warsaw. For matters relating to personal data, write to <link>hej@ciok.art</link>.
privacy.s2Li1: Data needed to fulfil an order — name, shipping address, email and phone number
privacy.s2Li2: The content of any message you send me by email
privacy.s2Li4: Payment data needed to complete your order — processed directly by <link>Stripe</link>; your full payment details never reach my servers
privacy.s2Li3: Basic technical browser data needed for the site and cart to work
privacy.s2P: I don’t collect data I don’t need, and I don’t sell it to anyone.
privacy.s3P: I process data to fulfil an order, reply to a message, handle payment and meet tax obligations. Payments are handled by <link>Stripe</link> as an external provider — I never see or store your full card details. The basis is performance of the contract and, for accounting, a legal obligation.
privacy.s4P: I keep order data for as long as tax regulations require. I delete email correspondence once the matter is settled, unless further correspondence requires keeping it.
privacy.s5P: The site uses essential cookies and browser storage to remember the contents of your cart. If you consent, analytics and marketing tools may also run. During checkout, <link>Stripe</link> sets its own cookies needed to process payment securely and prevent fraud.
privacy.s6P: You have the right to access your data, correct it, delete it and restrict its processing. Just write to me — I’ll reply as fast as I can.

fine-art-prints: Deep navy pools into translucent blue-green washes in 001, where a slender, finely striped curve draws the eye through the composition. A small golden disc and warm rust-coloured marks interrupt the cooler field, giving the work a poised balance between fluid movement and precise detail. Airy yet grounded, it brings quiet visual depth to a living room, bedroom, or focused workspace, whether displayed alone or alongside similarly restrained pieces.

A sweeping terracotta ribbon runs through 002, separating pale peach and teal washes from a concentrated pool of midnight blue. Fine contour lines, scattered coppery marks, and a single gold circle sharpen the contrast between softness and structure, creating an assured sense of motion. Its warm-cool palette can enliven a neutral living room or hallway while retaining enough delicacy for a quieter bedroom or study.

Two suspended fields of smoky blue, apricot, and pale green give 003 its open, almost weightless composition. A dark finely lined band sweeps across both forms, while rust-coloured traces, rippling contours, and a compact gold accent reward a closer look without disturbing the generous white space. The result is dynamic but uncluttered—a distinctive focal point for contemporary interiors that also pairs naturally with light woods and soft neutral textiles.

Soft blue washes meet olive radial forms in 004, setting delicate line work and lively green-blue speckles against generous white space. The contrast between translucent colour, taut curves, and fan-like geometry gives the composition a fresh, sculptural rhythm that shifts between calm and energy. Bright without feeling loud, this print makes an elegant focal point in a living room or studio and sits beautifully beside natural wood, stone, and muted textiles.

Layered bands of misty blue, moss green, and luminous yellow establish the bold graphic structure of 005. Finely radiating loops anchor the upper and lower edges, while loose black-and-white curves travel across the composition with an easy, animated rhythm. Its balance of broad colour and intricate line work brings confident warmth to a living room, dining area, or creative workspace, standing strongly on its own without overwhelming the space.

Concentric washes of smoky grey, soft peach, and deep navy gather into the rounded, stone-like form of 006. Fine burgundy stripes trace one edge while a small golden disc glows near the centre, balancing broad translucent colour with intricate detail. Quiet and enveloping, the composition brings a sense of depth to a bedroom, reading corner, or calm living space without losing the lightness of its generous white ground.

Warm peach and misty grey washes fold around a midnight-blue centre in 007, forming a softly layered, shell-like silhouette. A burgundy striped contour loops through the composition, joined by a golden circle and loose black gestures that lend precision and spontaneity in equal measure. Its centred balance and subtle glow make an elegant focal point for a bedroom, study, or living room shaped by warm woods and natural textures.

A broad terracotta form meets an oversized taupe oval in 008, creating a bold dialogue between saturated colour and finely radiating line work. Pale tendrils, soft dotted details, navy tabs, and quick black marks animate the surface without crowding its graphic structure. Playful yet composed, this print adds character to a dining area, hallway, or creative workspace and stands especially well against clean, neutral surroundings.

Pale grey and sand-coloured washes establish the measured geometry of 009, while charcoal pools and rust-toned speckles soften its rectangular structure. Two wavering vertical bands—one finely striped in blue, the other deep black—draw the eye downward as a delicate line arcs across the field. Calm but distinctive, the composition suits a study, hallway, or understated living room where its restrained rhythm can unfold gradually.

A sweeping navy loop cuts across 010, carrying the eye from a copper-toned oval into a broad field of blue-grey wash. Fine black lines, scattered rust marks, and freely dripped pigment heighten the contrast between controlled detail and spontaneous movement. Energetic without becoming busy, this print brings confident motion to a living room, studio, or workspace and pairs naturally with simple contemporary furnishings.

A tall striped arch in burgundy and navy frames the layered vertical forms of 011, where cool blue-grey washes meet touches of copper and rust. Long, fine curves cross the composition and a concentrated cloud of speckled colour gathers at the right, giving the work a sculptural upward rhythm. Its assured proportions make a striking addition to an entryway, dining area, or room with generous wall height.

A translucent copper arch sweeps over 012, meeting a dark, finely striped loop that curls from the lower edge into a generous oval. A navy block, delicate converging lines, and scattered warm speckles add weight and detail while leaving ample white space around the central movement. Bold yet airy, the composition introduces warmth and momentum to a living room, dining space, or creative studio.

Broad washes of stone, beige, and soft grey give 013 an architectural calm, punctuated by two slender burgundy striped columns. A deep blue block, pale circular pool, fine arcing lines, and scattered rust marks create depth within the otherwise restrained arrangement. Its strong vertical cadence and muted palette make it a refined focal point for a hallway, study, or contemporary living room.

Rust and cool blue washes rise through the open composition of 014, crossed by pale striped loops that curl, dip, and circle through the white space. Fine black arcs and densely speckled passages add a second, more intricate rhythm to the broad painterly forms. Lively but finely balanced, this print brings expressive movement to a studio, living room, or hallway while keeping the surrounding space feeling light.

A single irregular oval holds the dramatic contrasts of 015, shifting from deep rust and charcoal into an icy, textured blue. An electric cobalt ring hovers above a dark burst of pigment, with fine filaments and sharp white openings adding tension and lift. Striking yet contained, the work creates a memorable focal point in a living room, dining area, or minimal workspace.

Two upright fields of rust, peach, and pale blue stand apart in 016, connected by a looping band of finely drawn grey lines. A vivid cobalt stroke and delicate black arcs sharpen the composition, while the open centre keeps its movement light and spacious. Expressive without overwhelming a room, this print suits a bright hallway, creative workspace, or contemporary living area.

Luminous yellow-green washes meet smoky charcoal and olive in 017, creating a soft field of colour around a large pale radial ring. Fine white tendrils descend through the darker tones, ending among a cluster of hazy circular marks that reward a closer view. Glowing yet grounded, the composition brings gentle vitality to a bedroom, reading nook, or living room furnished in natural neutrals.

Two pale columns of grey-green and powder blue give 018 its airy vertical structure, separated by a clean channel of white. A curved navy band steadies the left side, while blue and rust granulation gathers along the right and fine black filaments rise from a charcoal bloom below. Delicate yet full of texture, this print lends quiet height to a bedroom, hallway, or contemplative workspace.

A muted field of beige and grey provides a hushed setting for the burgundy and navy striped ring in 019. Two soft charcoal blooms appear to float beside fine dangling lines, while dark pooled pigment and rust speckles add weight near the lower edge. Minimal but never empty, the composition offers a calm, intriguing presence for a bedroom, study, or softly furnished living room.

Translucent green-grey wash spreads across 020, opened by tall white slashes and a feathery burst of rust at the left. Overlapping ochre and burgundy rings anchor the opposite side, with pale blue dots and fine black filaments adding quiet complexity. The balance of earthy colour and graphic form gives this print an assured warmth suited to a dining room, hallway, or modern living space.

Soft cream and grey washes surround the finely striped navy ring of 021, which encloses a warm ochre pool near the lower edge. Hazy blue-charcoal circles, delicate trailing lines, and a rust-coloured cloud bring movement to the generous open field. Restrained and atmospheric, the work makes a thoughtful addition to a reading corner, bedroom, or calm living room where subtle details can be appreciated up close.

Vertical ribbons of lavender, pale yellow, blush, and smoky blue give 022 a tall, lyrical cadence. A vivid cobalt striped band rises along the right, while flowing black contours, dark rust gestures, and a small golden accent concentrate the eye near the centre. Graceful but confidently coloured, this print brings elegant height to an entryway, dining area, or contemporary bedroom.

Layered washes of blue-grey, amber, olive, and charcoal stretch horizontally across 023, creating a broad, horizon-like rhythm. Rust-toned clusters and dark green accents punctuate the upper field, while white threads and a finely striped band travel through the lower layers. Calm and expansive, the composition can visually open a living room, dining area, or hallway while adding warmth to a restrained interior.

Two luminous forms in periwinkle and deep cobalt stand side by side in 024, each shaped by dense radiating lines and curved bands. A dark blue pool gathers between them, while white openings, fine black contours, and two small golden accents keep the composition bright and precise. Cool, sculptural, and elegant, this print makes a distinctive focal point for a living room, bedroom, or polished workspace.

Three stacked forms give 025 its playful structure: a pale yellow field threaded with blue ribbons, a richly speckled terracotta ring, and a broad teal oval below. Fine black lines, a small red radial accent, and generous white openings keep the strong colour feeling light. Its balance of warmth, coolness, and graphic shape brings cheerful sophistication to a dining area, creative workspace, or contemporary living room.

Watery blue washes and soft bands of sand and peach unfold across 026 in a layered horizontal rhythm. Finely drawn waves cross the open upper field, while rust and pale blue striped ribbons travel through darker pools of pigment, joined by a slender golden accent. Expansive and atmospheric, the composition brings measured movement to a living room, hallway, or dining space without overpowering quieter surroundings.

Lavender and deep blue washes rise through 027, set against a pale inner glow and crisp flashes of cobalt. Fine lines arc along the tall forms, while a brown striped half-ring and a small golden mark introduce warmth and precision at opposite edges. Luminous and composed, this print adds elegant height to a bedroom, entryway, or living room with cool neutrals and natural materials.

A broad blue-grey arch meets a richly textured orange loop in 028, creating a bold interplay of cool openness and concentrated warmth. Rust-toned washes, two finely radiating rings, cream ribbons, and a dark splatter at the base build an energetic, sculptural arrangement. Confident and full of movement, this print makes a vivid focal point in a dining room, studio, or contemporary living space.

Tall washes of blue-grey and warm tan form the quiet foundation of 029, threaded by a pair of dark, finely striped loops. Repeated hairline arcs sweep through rust and blue speckles, while deeper navy and brown accents lend weight to the outer edges. Elegant and gently animated, the composition brings graceful vertical movement to a hallway, bedroom, or refined living area.

A pale periwinkle loop dominates 030, its soft translucent surface sharpened by a vivid cobalt arc of finely spaced lines. Beside it, a narrow charcoal and rust form carries dark gestures, delicate filaments, and a small golden detail near the lower edge. The contrast feels both poised and expressive, making this print a sophisticated focal point for a living room, study, or contemporary entryway.

A broad field of lavender floats above pale yellow in 031, divided by a dark horizontal wash and a vivid cobalt line that travels down the right. White openings, fine black curves, subtle rust speckles, and small golden accents bring intricate detail to the clear graphic structure. Serene yet unmistakably modern, the composition adds confident colour to a bedroom, workspace, or light-filled living room.

Pale periwinkle and misty grey washes frame the deep indigo centre of 032, where pigment blooms outward in rich, feathery textures. A vertical golden accent catches the eye among rust speckles and fine rising lines, while a softly striped oval steadies the upper corner. Atmospheric and luminous, this print brings quiet drama to a bedroom, reading space, or contemporary living room.

A blush-toned wash and bright blue speckles form the soft backdrop of 033, balanced by two finely radiating rings in rust and periwinkle. Cream curves overlap the upper forms, while a red sunburst expands from the lower corner with playful confidence. Graphic yet light-hearted, the composition brings warmth and character to a dining area, creative workspace, or welcoming living room.

A large wash of pale grey-green fills 034, deepening into charcoal along one edge and opening into quiet areas of white. Fine black curves descend through the field, accompanied by rust-toned speckles and a richly striped oval suspended above. Understated but full of subtle movement, this print offers a composed focal point for a bedroom, study, or calm contemporary living space.

Soft green-grey wash gives 035 an open, balanced foundation, interrupted by charcoal pooling and lively rust-coloured traces. A compact teal ring hovers at the upper edge, while a broad terracotta oval anchors the base with dense radiating lines and a luminous centre. Earthy and graphic in equal measure, the print brings grounded warmth to a dining room, hallway, or modern living area.

A pale blue-grey wash rises along the left of 036, textured with dark pooling and a delicate burst of blue and rust. A terracotta striped line sweeps overhead, curls tightly at the centre, then descends into a generous loop beside an expressive charcoal splash. Fluid and energetic, the composition lends striking movement to a living room, studio, or tall hallway wall.

Separated fields of rust, blush, and pale blue create the open architecture of 037, punctuated by a vivid cobalt stroke near the upper edge. A wide grey striped loop winds across both forms as fine black lines echo its movement through the surrounding white space. Dynamic yet airy, this print adds expressive scale to a living room, creative workspace, or spacious entryway.

A broad lavender field darkens into soft-edged brown and charcoal blooms in 038, crossed by slender vertical lines and a narrow cream striped band. A broken horizontal seam of dark pigment and gold separates the upper form from its pale, reflected counterpart below. Moody yet balanced, the composition brings atmospheric depth to a living room, dining area, or quiet study.

Pale blue and blush washes spread across 039 in a spacious, stepped formation, lifted by two saturated cobalt strokes at the upper left. Rust speckles and fine vertical lines descend toward a dark horizontal band, where flowing white contours create a gentle wave-like rhythm. Expansive and quietly vivid, this print adds a sense of openness to a living room, bedroom, or long hallway.

A wide grey-green loop opens the upper half of 040, paired with a dark teal ring of finely radiating lines. A concentrated rust band crosses the centre, while a large, delicately drawn oval below carries scattered warm marks through its pale surface. Balanced, graphic, and quietly earthy, the composition makes an assured focal point for a dining room, living area, or understated workspace.

Cool grey-green washes rise along one side of 041 as warm rust and terracotta marks gather on the other, leaving a generous channel of white between them. A dark teal striped ring crowns the cooler form, while feathery blooms and a pale pink stroke animate the warmer edge. Bold but beautifully balanced, this print brings expressive contrast to a hallway, studio, or contemporary living room.

printPdp.artistBio: Anna Ciok is a Warsaw-based artist who paints and makes ceramics; her work pairs bold colour with a handmade gesture. The prints in this collection reproduce her original paintings and are printed in an open edition on archival paper.
printPdp.accordionProductDetails:
Fine Art print on EMA 200 g/m² paper — a matte, archival-quality stock. Open edition.

Keep away from moisture and direct sunlight; wipe the frame with a dry cloth.
printPdp.accordionFraming: Every print is available unframed or in a wooden frame: black, light brown or dark brown.
printPdp.accordionShipping: Prints are produced and shipped by our partner Prodigi within 5–10 working days. We ship to home addresses in the European Union and the United Kingdom — parcel-locker delivery is not available. See the Delivery & returns page for return details.

giftCard.lead: Choose an amount and pay online — the code lands in your inbox right after payment. Redeem it for ceramics or fine-art prints on one future order.

giftCard.accordionHowBody:
Pick one of the four amounts and pay online.

Right after payment we email you a unique code — ready to print or forward as a message.

Enter the code in the "I have a promo code" field in the cart, on any ceramics or fine-art-print order.
giftCard.accordionTermsBody:
The code is single-use, for one future order. If your cart total is lower than the card's value, the remainder is forfeited — it is not refunded or carried forward to a later purchase.

The card never expires and can be used for either ceramics or fine-art prints.

Gift cards cannot be combined with other promo codes, and a gift card itself cannot be bought together with ceramics or prints in the same order.
